Commentary publishes short pieces in which scholars comment on populism and populist actors: an opinion, an argument, a way of looking at a question. The pieces are written by scholars and reviewed by the editor. Commentary appears quarterly.

:::

## Call for commentary

Commentary starts with invited pieces. Scholars who want to write are welcome too: send your piece to the editor at editor@populiverse.com

## Guidelines

**Who can write.** PhD holders and doctoral candidates, with their affiliation stated. The decision to publish is the editor's.

**What Commentary publishes.** Your view on a question about populism or populist actors: an opinion, an argument, an approach. No partisan advocacy.

**Length.** 800 to 1,500 words. The length is flexible.

**Pitch.** Each piece opens with a pitch of 100 to 150 words that says what the piece argues. It is printed at the top of the piece. Nothing has to be sent to the editor beforehand.

**Sources.** You choose the form: links in the text, author-date (Harvard) references, a reference list at the end, or none. The editor may ask for a source for a specific factual claim.

**Whose views.** Every piece carries a line saying that the views are the author's own.

**Review.** Pieces are editor-reviewed. Commentary is not peer-reviewed, and PopuliVerse does not describe it as such.

**What you send.** The piece, your affiliation, your ORCID iD and the declaration below, in one email to editor@populiverse.com

**Cost.** None. There is no fee to submit or to publish.

**How a piece is published.** As a web page and as a typeset PDF, with its own DOI and a "Cite this" box. It is also collected in the PDF of its issue.

**After publication.** Corrections and the right of reply are set out in the [editorial policy](../about/editorial-policy.qmd).

## The author's declaration

Copy the lines below into your email. In each group, keep the one line that applies to you.

**1. The piece**

- is new and has not been published
- builds on work of mine that is published or under review, which I name in the piece
- has appeared elsewhere, and I hold the right to republish it

**2. AI tools**

- were not used
- were used for language only (spelling, grammar, translation)
- were used in drafting; I have checked every sentence and I answer for the text

**3. Interests**

- I have no tie to any actor discussed in the piece
- I am or was a member, adviser or employee of a party, government or organisation discussed
- my work on this topic is or was funded by an actor discussed
- I have another tie, which I name in one line

**4. Licence**

- CC BY 4.0: anyone may share and adapt the piece, with credit to me
- CC BY-ND 4.0: anyone may share the piece, with credit to me, but not change it
- Not sure: the editor applies the site's standard, CC BY 4.0

**5. The views in the piece are my own.**

Keeping a line does not guarantee publication: the editor decides in each case. Authors keep the copyright in their pieces. What the licences allow is on the [licence page](../legal/licence.qmd).
